solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One gets credit in car club for decorative braid

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the first pair of pieces sits inside the club's letters

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the usual accounting abbreviation for credit
the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club member is praised for some ornamental trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British breakdown and motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricrac is a zigzag ribbon trimming sewn onto clothes, a kind of decorative braid.

clue.text: West Indian repelled one old despot

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so these words are read backwards

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
a Russian emperor of former times

explanation.surface: A Caribbean islander fought off a tyrant of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, short for Rastafarian, follows a religious movement that began in Jamaica, so is typically West Indian.

clue.text: Ceremony with tea that's served up by university

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for that is written bottom to top

blocks.note: cha is a slang word for tea
yon is an old or dialect word for that
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A formal ritual involving tea is laid on by a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nearly describes the answer, so it is semi-&lit: the definition is the ceremony, and the tea really is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanoyu is the Japanese tea ceremony, a formal ritual of preparing and serving powdered green tea.

clue.text: Female traffic warden turned up in area with international transport

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means the letters are written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
TIR, Transports Internationaux Routiers, is the international road haulage scheme seen on lorries

explanation.surface: A lady enforcing parking rules showed up at an international transport zone.
explanation.walkthrough: TIR plates appear on continental lorries crossing borders under the international customs scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely Rita is the meter maid of the Beatles song, making the name a byword for a female parking attendant.

clue.text: Lord's school dead reserved

indicators.note: something reserved is set aside, so that letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: a co-ed is a mixed school
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A peer's school has had its deceased kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The school loses its D to leave COE; Sebastian Coe, the Olympic runner, sits in the House of Lords as Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Coe is the life peerage title of the athlete and sports administrator Sebastian Coe.

clue.text: Opening with code right away, absorb stuff gradually

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is taken out of the code word

blocks.note: os is the anatomical term for an opening or mouth
the telegraph code of dots and dashes
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Starting with a cipher, the right way to take in material is slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening looks like the start of the sentence; here it is the anatomical word for a mouth or aperture.
explanation.definitionFit: To osmose is to pass through a membrane by osmosis, hence to take something in slowly and gradually.

clue.text: Burden of proof initially with some of the media

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the first letter of of
the first letter of proof
the press, newspapers, is part of the media

explanation.surface: The legal burden of proof is placed on journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites 'burden of proof' as one phrase; instead Burden is the definition and initially takes the first letters of both of and proof.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to weigh down or burden someone heavily, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: This works about right for "close covering"

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over and remade into a fresh order
about means going around, so the shuffled letters wrap round the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A remark that something is just about the right phrase for a snug covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt is a garment worn close to the body, a fitted covering for the torso.

clue.text: Yours truly's sullen with vertigo

blocks.note: yours truly is the setter, me; the 's means is
grim means gloomy or sullen

explanation.surface: The writer admits being glum while suffering from dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Megrim is an old word for migraine and also for vertigo or giddiness.

clue.text: Bosnia sent new clothes with Red Cross

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bosnia dispatched fresh garments with help from the Red Cross charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Cross looks like the aid charity; it describes the garment's red St Andrew's cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanbenito was the penitential tunic of the Spanish Inquisition, yellow and marked with a red saltire cross.

clue.text: More reduced insurance for tools

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: else means more, as in anything else
ins is the abbreviation for insurance

explanation.surface: Cheaper cover is taken out on equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More reduced' reads like a comparative adjective, but More is the word to be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An elsin is a Scots word for an awl, the shoemaker's pointed tool.

clue.text: I reckon hospitals hit badly — ignoring variant risk is not for me

indicators.note: badly suggests the long phrase is mangled into a different order
ignoring means leaving out, so a set of letters is taken away from the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written, the full pool of letters
any arrangement of these letters, variant marking them as free to move, is removed

explanation.surface: Someone cautious says hospitals are badly struck and gambling is not for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of RISK IS NOT out of the long phrase and shuffle the rest. Achitophel deserted King David for Absalom, so to David he is the man not for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Achitophel, David's counsellor who went over to the rebel Absalom, is the type of the treacherous adviser, one not on your side.

clue.text: Maori staff nurse joins hospital among cheers

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so the joined pieces go inside the word for cheers

blocks.note: an aia, or ayah, is a nursemaid in India
H is the abbreviation for hospital
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A New Zealand nursing worker enters a hospital to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maori staff' reads as Maori employees; staff is a long stick. Ta is everyday British slang for thank you, often rendered cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A taiaha is a traditional Maori fighting staff, a long wooden close-combat weapon.

clue.text: Dressed-up Romans love going out, scrambled egg on toast first of all

indicators.note: going out means leaving, so the letter standing for love is dropped
first of picks just the leading letter of the word that follows
scrambled means mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
love is a zero score, O
the first letter of all

explanation.surface: Romans in finery dine on scrambled egg on toast before love departs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one O out of egg on toast, add the A from all, and scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Gens togata, the toga-wearing race, is Virgil's phrase for the Romans, dressed in their formal toga.

clue.text: They succeed in shooting pigeons

indicators.note: shooting suggests something blasted apart, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people are good at bagging pigeons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They succeed' reads as they do well; here it means they come after.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigons are followers or successors, especially lesser imitators of a great generation.

clue.text: With little space in suite, work in front of curtain

indicators.note: in places the small space inside the word for the retinue

blocks.note: an en is a small printing space, half an em
a suite is a train of followers, a tail

explanation.surface: With a cramped hotel suite, someone works in front of a theatre curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre picture hides a fortification: work means a defensive earthwork, and the curtain is the wall between two bastions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenail, or tenaille, is a low outwork built in front of the curtain wall of a fortress.

clue.text: International bank backing India's spring crop

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the joined pieces are read from right to left

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for international
a bar is a sandbank

explanation.surface: A global bank supports India's harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabi is the Indian crop sown in autumn and harvested in spring, such as wheat or barley.

clue.text: Source of fruit coming with it locally

blocks.note: anon means soon, on the way
a is a dialect form of he, she or it

explanation.surface: Where fruit comes from arrives with local produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Anona, or annona, is the tropical tree genus that bears custard apples and soursops.

clue.text: Keen blogger, say uncertain regularly? Meditation needed ultimately

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of uncertain
Zen is the Buddhist school of meditation

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic blogger is unsure whether meditation is needed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed ultimately' says the meditation word comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A netizen is an active user of the internet, and a keen blogger is an example of one.

clue.text: Mentally prepares dodgy Dickens character on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the sound of the name counts

blocks.note: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Someone braces for a role as a shady figure from Dickens on a radio drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych someone up is to get them mentally ready, so psyches means mentally prepares.

clue.text: French stars going topless are hot in Riviera summer sun

indicators.note: topless means without a top, so the first letter is dropped
in puts the shortened word inside the French word for summer

blocks.note: été is French for summer, as spoken on the Riviera
to boil is to be very hot
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: Topless sunbathers on the French Riviera in summer get very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Riviera tells the solver to take summer in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Étoiles is French for stars, and also the top-ranking dancers of a French ballet company.

clue.text: Unbacked seat catches erect American soldier

indicators.note: unbacked means without its back end, so the last letter goes
erect in a down entry means standing upright, so the letters run bottom to top
catches means holds inside, so the shortened word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: nates are the buttocks, the seat
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A chair without a back holds an upright GI.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier here is a caste of termite, not a GI; seat is the buttocks, in their Latin anatomical name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasute is a soldier termite with a nozzle-like head that squirts sticky fluid at enemies.

clue.text: A lady going around city unclothed?

definitions.text: A lady going around city unclothed?

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of its outer layer, so only the inner letters stay
going around means surrounding, so the lady's letters enclose the stripped word

blocks.note: a plus dame, a lady
the inside letters of city

explanation.surface: A woman walks round town naked, like Lady Godiva.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a naked woman round the city is an Adamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamites were a sect who went naked in imitation of Adam, so an Adamite is a nudist.

clue.text: Hawks beginning to shoot inspiring end of western

indicators.note: to shoot means to go up fast, and in a down entry up means bottom to top
inspiring means breathing in, so the word takes the letter inside it
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'western'

blocks.note: a start is a beginning
the last letter of western

explanation.surface: Birds of prey start firing at the end of a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawks looks like the birds; it is a verb meaning peddles.
explanation.definitionFit: To trant is an old word for to peddle goods about, so trants means hawks.

clue.text: Batted flipping insect not seen before

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so both pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: a nit is a louse egg
something new has not been seen before

explanation.surface: Someone swatted a never-before-seen bug in irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: Batted looks like swatting; in cricket, the side batting has gone in.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman goes in to bat, so a side that went in batted.

clue.text: Jewish leader sat out with clergyman? That's one side of Qatar

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order
one side of takes an outer letter, here the first, of the country

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of Qatar

explanation.surface: A rabbi sat out with a cleric, asking whether that is one side of Qatar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsaddiq is a righteous man, the title of a Hasidic spiritual leader.

clue.text: US bass singer dressed for ceremony?

blocks.note: first meaning: Paul ..., the American bass and actor
second meaning, read as two words: wearing formal gowns

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split: read as two words, the singer's surname says the robes are on.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was the celebrated American bass singer of Ol' Man River, and robes on describes someone in ceremonial dress.

clue.text: Fleet Street's written about old woman oozing eccentricity

indicators.note: oozing means leaking out, so that letter escapes from the word
written about means set down around, so the street's letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
an old woman is slang for one's wife
e is the mathematical symbol for eccentricity

explanation.surface: Fleet Street has reported on an odd elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district, suggests journalism; Fleet alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast-moving, quick on its feet, and so does swift.

clue.text: Settle in Italy, say

blocks.note: first meaning: to fix or settle, an older verb sense
second meaning: a nation, of which Italy is an example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests emigrating to Italy; Chambers gives state as a verb meaning to settle or fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is an example of a sovereign nation, and to state is an old verb meaning to fix or establish.

clue.text: Use crack to relieve pressure

indicators.note: to relieve of something is to take it away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: crack as an adjective means highly skilled
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Open a crack to let off pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack looks like a split; here it is the adjective, as in a crack shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence or strength is to use it, bringing it to bear.

clue.text: Front removed from car in struggle

indicators.note: front removed means the first letter is taken off the vehicle word

blocks.note: a wagon is a railway car or estate car

explanation.surface: Someone tears the front off a car during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Agon is the Greek word for a contest or conflict, used in English for a struggle.

clue.text: Clumsy idiot fathoms out puzzle

indicators.note: out means removed, so that unit's abbreviation leaves the word

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fathoms
to flummox is to baffle

explanation.surface: A bungling fool works out a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fathoms out' looks like figures out; it splits as fathoms, out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is an awkward, slow-witted person, a lumbering oaf.

clue.text: Some supporting Sondheim's finale in vintage Company

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so only the last letter of the name is kept
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the word for some goes second, below

blocks.note: the last letter of Sondheim
any means some, as in have you any?

explanation.surface: Some performers appeared in the closing number of a revival of Sondheim's musical Company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, supporting puts the word for some under the letter M. Company is Sondheim's musical but here means a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: Many, from meinie, is an obsolete noun for a household or retinue, an old word for a company of people.

clue.text: Piscina utilised only partly for swimmers

indicators.note: only partly means just a portion of the phrase is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A swimming pool was only partly used by bathers.
explanation.walkthrough: A piscina is a fishpond or pool, which feeds the swimming picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautili are the shelled cephalopods of the ocean, which swim by jet propulsion.

clue.text: Indian mister turned up for tax collectors

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means the letters are written bottom to top

blocks.note: Sri is an Indian title of respect, like Mr

explanation.surface: An Indian gentleman arrived to see the taxmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The IRS, the Internal Revenue Service, is the United States federal tax agency.

clue.text: Inmate's record shows person enjoying rights forever

blocks.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence; the 's means has
to enter is to record in a register

explanation.surface: A prisoner's criminal record reveals someone with permanent entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: Forever here means for the rest of a life, not for all time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a liferenter holds a liferent, the right to use property for the duration of their life.

clue.text: Stokes gossips as before with exceptional people in Perth?

blocks.note: S is the symbol for the stokes, a unit of viscosity
aunt is an obsolete word for a gossip or old woman

explanation.surface: A man named Stokes chats with some remarkable Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth suggests Australia, but it is the Scottish city: saunt is Scots for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saunts is the Scots form of saints, the most virtuous of people.

clue.text: Most timid getting jab indeed for nothing

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one word is swapped in where the other was

blocks.note: a shot is an injection, a jab
yes, indeed, as an affirmation
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The most nervous patient is offered a vaccination for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for nothing' reads as free of charge; here the word for indeed replaces the O in the jab word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyest is the superlative of shy, meaning the most bashful or timid.
